questions.statement: Choose the sentence that is grammatically correct in the present simple.
questions.context: Examen de gramatica en El Salvador, grado 11.

options.text: She work at a pharmacy on Saturdays.
options.feedback: Missing the third person singular -s: it would have to be 'She works'.

options.text: She works at a pharmacy on Saturday.
options.feedback: The habitual action happens every Saturday, so the day must be plural: 'on Saturdays'.

options.text: She is work at a pharmacy on Saturdays.
options.feedback: Mixing two present forms: the verb cannot be both 'is' and the bare 'work'.

options.text: She works at a pharmacy on Saturdays.
options.feedback: Third person singular takes -s in the present simple, so this form is correct.

questions.explanation:
En presente simple, el verbo cambia su terminacion segun el sujeto: -s en he/she/it, -0 en I/you/we/they. Solo la opcion B respeta esa regla.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'Water ____ at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.'
questions.context: Practica de presente simple en la clase de ingles de San Salvador.

options.text: boil
options.feedback: The plural -s of the noun 'water' is not transferred to the verb; 'boils' is required.

options.text: is boiling
options.feedback: Present continuous describes an action in progress right now, not a scientific constant.

options.text: boiled
options.feedback: Simple past refers to a completed action in the past, not to a permanent property.

options.text: boils
options.feedback: Incontable subject + present simple: add -s, so 'water boils'.

questions.explanation:
El enunciado habla de una verdad general y el sujeto 'water' es incontable, por lo que se usa el verbo 'boil' en tercera persona singular.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question is correctly formed in the present simple?
questions.context: Evaluacion de estructuras interrogativas, grado 11.

options.text: Do she live near the university?
options.feedback: 'Do' goes with I, you, we and they; with 'she' it must be 'Does'.

options.text: Does she lives near the university?
options.feedback: After 'does' the verb stays in the base form; adding -s would double the third person mark.

options.text: Does she live near the university?
options.feedback: 'Does' takes the base form 'live' and carries the -s of the third person singular.

options.text: Is she lives near the university?
options.feedback: 'Is' cannot open a question with a main verb like 'live' in the simple present.

questions.explanation:
En preguntas del presente simple el auxiliar do se usa en tercera persona singular (does) y el verbo principal vuelve a su forma base.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative sentence.
questions.context: Practica de negacion en presente simple, San Miguel.

options.text: My brother do not play chess on Fridays.
options.feedback: The auxiliary must agree with the subject; with 'brother' it must be 'does not'.

options.text: My brother not play chess on Fridays.
options.feedback: The negative needs a full auxiliary ('does not'), not a bare 'not' before the verb.

options.text: My brother does not plays chess on Fridays.
options.feedback: After 'does not' the verb returns to its base form: 'does not play'.

options.text: My brother does not play chess on Fridays.
options.feedback: 'Does not' + base verb is the correct negative for the third person singular.

questions.explanation:
Para negar en presente simple se usa 'do not' / 'does not' seguido del verbo en forma base. La forma correcta es la que coloca 'does not' delante de 'play'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'My father works in San Salvador, but he ____ three languages.' Choose the correct verb.
questions.context: Ejercicio de contraste de personas del verbo, grado 11.

options.text: speaks
options.feedback: The subject is 'he', so the third person singular form 'speaks' is required.

options.text: speak
options.feedback: The base form is used with I, you, we and they, but not with 'he'.

options.text: is speak
options.feedback: Mixing an auxiliary with a bare verb: only one present form can carry the tense.

options.text: speaking
options.feedback: 'Speaking' is a gerund or a present participle; it cannot be the only verb of the clause.

questions.explanation:
El sujeto de la segunda oracion es 'he', en tercera persona singular, asi que el verbo lleva -s en presente simple.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is true according to the information given? 'Sofia ____ her grandparents every Sunday.'
questions.context: Comprension de una rutina familiar, grado 11.

options.text: is visiting
options.feedback: Present continuous would place the visits at this moment, not every Sunday.

options.text: will visit
options.feedback: 'Will' describes a future action, but the routine is already established.

options.text: visits
options.feedback: A repeated weekly habit belongs to the present simple with -s for 'Sofia'.

options.text: has visited
options.feedback: Present perfect would link the visits to a past result or to an unspecified time.

questions.explanation:
El enunciado describe una rutina semanal: un hecho habitual y general, que se expresa en presente simple.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Fill in the blank with the correct form of 'to be': 'The students ____ in the classroom right now.'
questions.context: Practica del verbo 'to be' en tiempo presente, San Salvador.

options.text: is
options.feedback: Reserved for the singular 'he/she/it' or for 'this/that'.

options.text: are
options.feedback: Plural subject plus present continuous marker 'right now': 'are'.

options.text: am
options.feedback: Used only with the first person singular 'I'.

options.text: be
options.feedback: The bare infinitive cannot function as the verb of a declarative sentence.

questions.explanation:
La expresion 'right now' pide el presente continuo, y el verbo 'to be' conjugado con 'the students' es 'are'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly uses the present simple with a time expression?
questions.context: Evaluacion deexpresiones temporales, grado 11.

options.text: The shop is opening at eight every morning.
options.feedback: Present continuous with 'every morning' describes something temporary, not a fixed schedule.

options.text: The shop opened at eight every morning.
options.feedback: Simple past is incompatible with the repeated present habit 'every morning'.

options.text: The shop opens at eight every morning.
options.feedback: 'Every morning' marks a habitual action, so the present simple is the right tense.

options.text: The shop will open at eight every morning.
options.feedback: 'Will' refers to the future; the store schedule is already a fact.

questions.explanation:
Las expresiones como 'every', 'usually' o 'on Mondays' indican的习惯 y por tanto exigen presente simple.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text: 'El Salvador is in Central America. It has 18 departments.' Which tense describes the second sentence?
questions.context: Analisis de texto informativo, grado 11.

options.text: Present continuous
options.feedback: Present continuous would imply the fact is temporary or changing now.

options.text: Present simple
options.feedback: Permanent geographical facts are expressed in the present simple.

options.text: Past simple
options.feedback: Past simple would suggest the information is no longer valid.

options.text: Present perfect
options.feedback: Present perfect usually connects past actions to a present result, not static facts.

questions.explanation:
'It has' es una verdad geografica permanente, por lo que el verbo aparece en presente simple con tercera persona singular.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which option completes the sentence correctly? 'The children ____ their homework after school.'
questions.context: Practica de rutinas con sujeto plural, grado 11.

options.text: do
options.feedback: Plural subject uses 'do' with the base form 'do their homework'.

options.text: does
options.feedback: 'Does' is reserved for he/she/it; with a plural subject it would be incorrect.

options.text: are do
options.feedback: Mixing an auxiliary and a bare verb: only one form may carry the action.

options.text: doing
options.feedback: A gerund cannot stand alone as the verb of the sentence.

questions.explanation:
Un sujeto plural como 'the children' en tercera persona plural no lleva -s: se usa 'do' con la forma base.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that correctly uses a third person singular subject.
questions.context: Revision deFlexion verbal, grado 11.

options.text: The nurses watches over the patients at night.
options.feedback: Plural subject 'The nurses' requires the base form 'watch'.

options.text: The nurse watch over the patients at night.
options.feedback: Missing the -s of the third person singular.

options.text: The nurses is watch over the patients at night.
options.feedback: Combines the plural auxiliary 'are' idea with a bare verb; inconsistent.

options.text: The nurse watches over the patients at night.
options.feedback: 'The nurse' is third person singular, so the verb takes -s.

questions.explanation:
Solo la oracion con 'watch' tiene un sujeto en tercera persona singular ('The nurse') y por eso el verbo lleva -s.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.context: Consolidacion del presente simple, Santa Ana.

options.text: Traffic in the capital gets worse every rainy season.
options.feedback: Correct subject-verb agreement plus a habitual time expression.

options.text: Traffic in the capital getting worse every rainy season.
options.feedback: There is no finite verb: 'getting' alone cannot close the clause.

options.text: Traffic in the capital is get worse every rainy season.
options.feedback: 'Get worse' is not a progressive form; use 'gets worse'.

options.text: Traffic in the capital get worst every rainy season.
options.feedback: 'Worst' is the superlative, not the comparative required by 'get worse'.

questions.explanation:
El presente simple exige un verbo principal en forma finita, sin auxiliares que no correspondan y con la terminacion correcta del sujeto.

questions.statement: Look at the sentence and identify the error: 'My friends live in Mejicano, so they visit me often.' What is wrong with it?
questions.context: Deteccion de errores en presente simple, grado 11.

options.text: 'Live' should be 'lives' because the subject is plural.
options.feedback: The rule is the opposite: plural subjects take the base form without -s.

options.text: There is no error: plural subject with the base verb 'live'.
options.feedback: The agreement 'friends ... live' is correct, so nothing has to be changed.

options.text: 'Live' should be 'living' because the sentence describes a habit.
options.feedback: Habits go in the present simple, not the present continuous.

options.text: 'They' should be 'he' because one friend is mentioned.
options.feedback: The plural 'friends' and the plural pronoun 'they' are coherent with each other.

questions.explanation:
La oracion es correcta: 'friends' es plural, 'live' no lleva -s y la segunda proposicion mantiene la coherencia.

questions.statement: Which of these activities happens according to the text? 'Maria gets up at five, has breakfast and walks to school.'
questions.context: Comprension lectora de una rutina diaria, grado 11.

options.text: She walks to school.
options.feedback: 'Walks' is in the text and describes her way to school.

options.text: She drives to school.
options.feedback: The text says she walks; driving never appears.

options.text: She has lunch at school.
options.feedback: The text mentions breakfast at home, not lunch at school.

options.text: She studies at night.
options.feedback: No evening activity is described in the text.

questions.explanation:
El texto enumera tres acciones presente simple: levantarse, desayunar y caminar a la escuela.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is punctuated and worded correctly?
questions.context: Revision de estructuras simples, grado 11.

options.text: Water boil at one hundred degrees Celsius.
options.feedback: Missing the third person singular -s after 'boil'.

options.text: Water do boil at one hundred degrees Celsius.
options.feedback: 'Do' is the auxiliary of the emphatic form, not of the plain affirmative.

options.text: Water are boiling at one hundred degrees Celsius.
options.feedback: Wrong auxiliary and wrong tense for a permanent physical fact.

options.text: Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius.
options.feedback: Subject plus base verb in the present simple: no auxiliary is needed.

questions.explanation:
Una oracion afirmativa en presente simple con sujeto y verbo correctamente concordados no lleva ningun auxiliar.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct translation: 'Los estudiantes llegan temprano todos los dias.'
questions.context: Traduccion de rutinas, de español a ingles, grado 11.

options.text: The students arriving early every day.
options.feedback: Non-finite form: 'arriving' cannot be the verb of the sentence.

options.text: The students arrive early every day.
options.feedback: Habitual action in the present simple with third person -s and 'every day'.

options.text: The students arrived early every day.
options.feedback: Simple past would refer to a finished action, not a daily habit.

options.text: The students is arriving early every day.
options.feedback: Subject-verb agreement error: plural 'students' takes 'arrive'.

questions.explanation:
'Llegan' es tercera persona singular en presente simple, por eso en ingles aparece 'arrive' con -s; 'every day' traduce 'todos los dias'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question would you use to ask about a habit that starts with 'do'?
questions.context: Formulacion de preguntas sobre habitos, grado 11.

options.text: Do you eat breakfast every morning?
options.feedback: 'Do' + subject + base verb is the standard present simple question.

options.text: Do you eating breakfast every morning?
options.feedback: After 'do' the verb must be in the base form, not the gerund.

options.text: Are you eat breakfast every morning?
options.feedback: 'Are' cannot be the auxiliary of the main verb 'eat' here.

options.text: Did you eat breakfast every morning?
options.feedback: 'Did' asks about a past action, not about a daily habit.

questions.explanation:
Para preguntar por una accion habitual se usa 'Do' seguido del sujeto y del verbo en forma base.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The children ____ (play) football every Saturday. Choose the correct option.
questions.context: Aplicacion de presente simple con sujeto plural, grado 11.

options.text: plays
options.feedback: The -s ending belongs to he/she/it, not to a plural subject.

options.text: is play
options.feedback: Illegal combination of an auxiliary and a bare verb.

options.text: play
options.feedback: Plural subject requires the base form of the verb.

options.text: are played
options.feedback: Passive voice is impossible here: the children are the ones who play.

questions.explanation:
'The children' es plural, de modo que el verbo aparece en forma base sin terminacion -s.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Identify the time expression that requires the present simple in the sentence: 'They ____ to the cinema every Friday.'
questions.context: Analisis de marcadores temporales, grado 11.

options.text: right now
options.feedback: 'Right now' would require the present continuous.

options.text: every Friday
options.feedback: 'Every' plus a day of the week marks a recurring habit and forces the present simple.

options.text: yesterday
options.feedback: 'Yesterday' is a past time marker and requires the simple past.

options.text: tomorrow
options.feedback: 'Tomorrow' points to the future and requires a future form.

questions.explanation:
'Every Friday' es un marcador de frecuencia habitual que obliga al presente simple.

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly states a fact with a singular third person subject?
questions.context: Sintesis de presente simple, San Miguel.

options.text: The volcano Izalco erupt every few years.
options.feedback: Missing the third person singular -s on 'erupt'.

options.text: The volcanos Izalco erupts every few years.
options.feedback: Plural noun with a singular verb; the agreement is inconsistent.

options.text: The volcano Izalco erupts every few years.
options.feedback: 'Izalco' is singular and 'erupts' carries the third person -s.

options.text: The volcano Izalco are erupts every few years.
options.feedback: Combines a plural auxiliary with a conjugated form; grammatically impossible.

questions.explanation:
La unica opcion con sujeto en tercera persona singular y verbo correctamente terminado en -s es la correcta.
